title: Alternaria sinaloensis sp. nov., A New Species Causing Foliar Blight of Tree Tobacco (Nicotiana glauca G) in Sinaloa, Mexico
content: Alternaria sinaloensis is described as a new species causing foliar blight on tree tobacco (Nicotiana glauca) in Sinaloa, Mexico. The study included disease evaluation at 35 sampling sites, where incidence ranged from 30 to 80% and severity from 5 to 20% of diseased foliage area. The pathogen was isolated from symptomatic leaves, and 20 single-spore isolates were obtained for morphological, cultural, phylogenetic, and pathogenic characterization. On tree tobacco and in culture, the fungus produced large conidia with an obclavate body and a long beak, which placed it in Alternaria section Porri. Phylogenetic analysis of the gpd, calmodulin, and plasma membrane ATPase genes confirmed that the isolates represent a new species, distinct from other Alternaria species reported on solanaceous hosts. In pathogenicity tests, all isolates caused disease on tree tobacco and on tomato, although with variability in virulence within each host. However, there was no correlation between pathogenicity rankings of isolates on tobacco compared to those on tomato (rs = 0.022), indicating differential virulence in both hosts. The ability of A. sinaloensis to cause early blight symptoms on tomato under controlled conditions suggests a potential risk for this crop in the region, warranting monitoring in commercial fields and pathogenicity studies on other solanaceous crops.
